title: Affine Gabber effacement (Stacks 09ZE)
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal; put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $i:Z\to X$ be the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] induced by $A\to A/I$ (every closed subscheme of the affine scheme $X$ is of this form). Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on $X_{\Et}$, i.e. a torsion object of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $q>0$ and let $\xi\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F)$ be a class of etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of the inverse image $i^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then there are a torsion abelian sheaf $F'$ on $X_{\Et}$ and a monomorphism $\iota:F\to F'$ of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ such that $H^q(i^{-1}\iota)(\xi)=0$ in $H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F')$, where $H^q(\varphi)$ is the map induced on cohomology by a morphism of sheaves $\varphi$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. (This is Stacks' statement: $X$ affine, $Z\subseteq X$ any closed subscheme; no henselian hypothesis is needed. In particular it holds for every henselian pair $(A,I)$ and for $I=0$, $Z=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}$, the two cases used in the proof of Gabber's theorem 09ZI.)

proof.text: Scope: this route proves the existing attached Lean declaration for henselian pairs and Λ-module sheaves; it does not prove the stronger non-henselian abelian statement of this node. Represent the given closed-fibre class by a bounded Λ-module sheaf G mapping to F. Use the already proved torsion filtered-colimit construction, forgetting of coefficient colimits, inverse image preservation of colimits, etale filtered continuity, and the natural H/derived-cohomology isomorphism. Lift the small index category through ULift, and use Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep.

Choose an injective presentation G to J in Λ-module sheaves. If n annihilates G, its injection factors through E=kernel(n id_J), giving a monomorphism a:G to E. Cancellation by the kernel inclusion shows that n annihilates E, so E is torsion on geometric stalks. Bounded abelian surjectivity lifts the represented fibre class to X. The underlying abelian cohomology of E on X is zero in positive degree. Naturality of cohomological restriction therefore shows that a kills the fibre class.

Push out a:G to E along b:G to F. The pushout inclusion F to P is monic. E direct-sum F is torsion: its stalk is the direct sum of their torsion stalks, computed using preservation of biproducts. The canonical map E direct-sum F to P is epic, so P is torsion by the existing IsTorsionSheaf.of_epi theorem. The pushout equation and H.map_comp_apply give the vanishing of the original class.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$,
$T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $F$ be a
sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ which is torsion
[def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], with restriction $F_0$ to $T_0$. Every class
$c\in H^q(T_0,F_0)$ with $q>0$ admits a monomorphism $F\hookrightarrow F'$ into a
torsion sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules $F'$ such that the image of $c$ in
$H^q(T_0,F'_0)$ is zero.

proof.text:
*Step 1: a bounded representative.* $F$ is the filtered union of its subsheaves
$F[n]$ killed by $n$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], inverse image to $T_0$
commutes with this colimit, and cohomology of the quasi-compact quasi-separated
scheme $T_0$ commutes with filtered colimits. Hence there are a sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules $G$ with $nG=0$ for some $n\geq1$, a morphism $b:G\to F$ and a
class $z\in H^q(T_0,G_0)$ with $b_0(z)=c$.

*Step 2: lifting $z$ to $T$.* For an abelian sheaf $G$ killed by $n$, restriction
$H^q(T,G)\to H^q(T_0,G_0)$ is surjective. Indeed, regard $G$ as a sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/n$-modules. A closed-fibre class of a $\mathbf Z/n$-sheaf comes from a
constructible $\mathbf Z/n$-sheaf $C$ mapping to it
[lemma-weil-pbc-constructible-approximation]; $C$ embeds into a finite sum of
direct images of finite constant sheaves along finite finitely presented maps
[lemma-weil-pbc-constructible-finite-pushforward]; each component of the class is
killed by a finite finitely presented cover;
pushing out along $C\to G$ [lemma-weil-pbc-pushout-monicity] gives a
monomorphism of $\mathbf Z/n$-sheaves $G\hookrightarrow G'$ killing the class.
With this effacement, induction on $q$ in the long exact cohomology sequences of
$0\to G\to G'\to G'/G\to0$ on $T$ and on $T_0$ (degree zero being
[lemma-weil-pbc-etale-degree-zero]) shows that restriction is bijective for all
$\mathbf Z/n$-sheaves in all degrees, in particular surjective. Choose
$x\in H^q(T,G)$ restricting to $z$.

*Step 3: an acyclic target.* Embed $G$ into an injective sheaf $J$ of
$\Lambda$-modules and let $E=\ker(n:J\to J)$. Since $nG=0$ the embedding factors
through a monomorphism $a:G\hookrightarrow E$. The sheaf $E$ is killed by $n$,
hence torsion, and $H^q(T,E)=0$ for $q>0$: $E$ is an injective sheaf of
$\Lambda/n$-modules, because $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda/n}(-,E)=
\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,J)$ on sheaves of $\Lambda/n$-modules, and injective
sheaves of modules are acyclic. Therefore the image of $z$ in
$H^q(T_0,E_0)$, which is the restriction of the image of $x$ in $H^q(T,E)=0$,
vanishes.

*Step 4: pushout.* Let $F'=F\amalg_GE$ be the pushout of $b$ and $a$. Since $a$ is
a monomorphism, so is $F\to F'$ [lemma-weil-pbc-pushout-monicity], and $F'$ is a
quotient of the torsion sheaf $F\oplus E$, hence torsion. The image of
$c=b_0(z)$ in $H^q(T_0,F'_0)$ equals the image of $a_0(z)=0$ under
$E\to F'$, so it is zero.
